classification.difficultyReason: Substitute the supplied symbolic axis value and simplify to the stated vertex formula, then apply both explicitly requested vertex methods.

content.prompt: The parabola $y=ax^2+bx+c$ has an axis of symmetry at $x=-\dfrac{b}{2a}$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use this value to show that the vertex of the parabola is $V=\left(-\dfrac{b}{2a},-\dfrac{\Delta}{4a}\right)$.

answer.short:
$V=\left(-\dfrac{b}{2a},-\dfrac{\Delta}{4a}\right)$, where $\Delta=b^2-4ac$.

Substituting the axis value into the quadratic gives the vertex ordinate.

children.label: b
children.prompt: For each of the following quadratics, use the formula in part a to find the axis of symmetry. Then find the coordinates of the vertex, first by substitution into the quadratic, then using the formula in part a.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}x_V&=-\frac{4}{2(1)}\\x_V&=-2\end{aligned}$$
By substitution:
$$\begin{aligned}y_V&=(-2)^2+4(-2)+1\\y_V&=-3\end{aligned}$$
Using part a:
$$\begin{aligned}\Delta&=4^2-4(1)(1)\\\Delta&=12\\y_V&=-\frac{12}{4(1)}\\y_V&=-3\end{aligned}$$
Both methods give $V=(-2,-3)$.

$$\begin{aligned}x_V&=-\frac{-6}{2(1)}\\x_V&=3\end{aligned}$$
By substitution:
$$\begin{aligned}y_V&=3^2-6(3)+10\\y_V&=1\end{aligned}$$
Using part a:
$$\begin{aligned}\Delta&=(-6)^2-4(1)(10)\\\Delta&=-4\\y_V&=-\frac{-4}{4(1)}\\y_V&=1\end{aligned}$$
Both methods give $V=(3,1)$.

$$\begin{aligned}x_V&=-\frac{-12}{2(-3)}\\x_V&=-2\end{aligned}$$
By substitution:
$$\begin{aligned}y_V&=-3(-2)^2-12(-2)+1\\y_V&=-12+24+1\\y_V&=13\end{aligned}$$
Using part a:
$$\begin{aligned}\Delta&=(-12)^2-4(-3)(1)\\\Delta&=156\\y_V&=-\frac{156}{4(-3)}\\y_V&=13\end{aligned}$$
Both methods give $V=(-2,13)$.
